verses.1: In Iconium, they went there in order to join together with the Jews. They spoke in such a way that a large number of both Jews and Greeks believed in them.
verses.2: And those who were tried by the Jews brought back the souls of the nations to their rightful place, according to their brothers’ wills.
verses.3: They indeed spent a long time mocking him, while he continued to speak about the grace of God. He also showed signs and wonders that came from his hands.
verses.4: The crowd of people in the city split into two groups: some were with the Jews, and others were with the apostles.
verses.5: But as for the efforts of the nations, and also of the Jews along with their leaders, they tried to become arrogant and tyrannical.
verses.6: They fled to the cities of Lycia: Lystra and Derbe, as well as the surrounding areas.
verses.8: And there was a man who was unable to stand among the people in Lystros. He had a protruding belly from his mother’s pregnancy, and he never could sit still.
verses.9: He heard Paul speaking. He noticed that Paul had faith in his own salvation.
verses.10: He said in a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet.” Then he laughed and waved his hand.
verses.11: And when the crowd saw what Paul had done, they cried out in outrage against him, saying, “The gods have become like humans and have descended to our level.”
verses.12: They also called Barnabas “Dia”, and Paul “Hermon”, because he was the one who was known for his wisdom.
verses.13: The priests of the God who exists before the city planted statues and decorations on the gates, along with the crowd, in order to offer sacrifices.
verses.14: When the apostles heard Barnabas and Paul, they rushed out of their rooms into the crowd, shouting.
verses.15: And they said, “Men, why do you do these things? We, who share the same passions as you, want to help you return to God, who created heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them.”
verses.16: In those generations, he made sure that all the nations followed their own paths.
verses.17: Although he did not do good deeds for himself, yet from heaven he gives you fruits of various kinds, as well as food and happiness for your hearts.
verses.18: And by saying these things, they finally managed to stop the crowd from not offering sacrifices to them.
verses.19: Then, Jews from Antioche and Ikonium also came there. They persuaded the crowd and captured Paul outside the city, thinking that he had died.
verses.20: Then, he went into the city, surrounded by his disciples. In the evening, he went to Derbium with Barnabas.
verses.21: The missionaries also preached to those cities. After teaching them properly, they were sent back to Lystra, Ikonion, and Antiochean.
verses.22: Considering the souls of our disciples, we earnestly request that they be given faith. We also believe that, due to many sufferings, it is necessary for us to enter into the kingdom of God.
verses.23: Then, after they had been addressed by the elders in the assembly, they were given to the Lord, according to what they believed.
verses.24: And after passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
verses.25: And while they were speaking in Perga, they went down to Attaleia.
verses.26: From there, they went to Antiocheion. From there, they were assigned to the task that God had given them to carry out.
verses.27: And as they gathered the congregation together, they reported all that God had done among them, and how He had opened doors of faith for various nations.
verses.28: He also spent a long time with his disciples, not a little at all.
